meta.title: Navajo Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 145 expressions · 19 greetings, 36 everyday, 25 exclamations, 27 set expressions, 38 sentences · both directions
meta.desc: 145 Navajo expressions in five subdecks: 19 greetings and wishes, 36 everyday phrases, 25 exclamations, 27 set expressions and 38 short sentences. Both study directions come as cards of their own: Navajo → English (see the expression, recall its meaning) and English → Navajo (see the meaning, recall the expression). This is not a CEFR level; it is the set phrases a learner needs whole, which a word list cannot teach, and nothing here is taught by any of the level decks. The greetings are the everyday openings (yáʼátʼééh abíní 'good morning', haash yinílyé? 'what is your name?'), the thanks and the wishes for a birthday, Christmas and the New Year; the everyday phrases ask and answer where you are from, your clan, your age and the time, and say you are hungry, tired or ill; the set expressions are the many phrases built on tʼáá ('just, only') and tʼáadoo ('without') that Navajo uses where English has one word. WHERE THEY COME FROM: the 107 expressions of the first four subdecks are English Wiktionary's own Navajo entries, with its meanings, and 16 of them its pronunciation in the International Phonetic Alphabet; 8 come with an example sentence. The 38 sentences are Tatoeba's, each with its contributor's English, written as they wrote them except that the glottal stop is printed ʼ throughout. THERE ARE NO PROVERBS: neither English Wiktionary nor Tatoeba holds a Navajo proverb, and one written from memory would have no source. There is no read-aloud button: no device carries a Navajo voice. Sources. English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
